name: PDF Expert
subcategory: PDF editing, document workflows and electronic signatures
tagline: Annotate, fill, merge, and lightly edit PDFs in a polished local desktop app

pricing.notes: Annual subscription divided by 12; App Store pricing can vary.

tiers.name: Weekly
tiers.limits: iPhone, iPad and Mac; Premium features including OCR, conversion, editing and PDF Copilot
tiers.notes: The live official site localized to £4.99/week (about $6.75/week using the ECB 2026-08-12 reference rates); the official US App Store did not expose which listed USD in-app-purchase SKU maps to the weekly plan.

tiers.name: Yearly
tiers.limits: iPhone, iPad and Mac; major updates/new features, PDF Copilot, OCR, conversion and editing
tiers.notes: The official US App Store lists $79.99/year; the live website localized to £72.99/year, showing that regional storefront pricing differs. Includes a 30-day money-back guarantee.

tiers.name: Lifetime
tiers.limits: Mac only; one-time $139.99; ongoing fixes, but future major tools may cost extra
tiers.notes: The official US App Store lists a one-time $139.99 purchase; the live website localized to £129.99. One-time purchase, not a subscription.

pricing.freeTierCaps: Free download supports basic reading/annotation/form use; official page does not publish numeric free-use caps
pricing.billingTerms: weekly + annual ($79.99/year in the US App Store) + $139.99 lifetime Mac-only; annual/lifetime have a 30-day guarantee; storefront pricing varies by region
pricing.hiddenCosts: Lifetime does not cover iPhone/iPad and future major features may require another fee. Weekly USD pricing was not identifiable from the US App Store SKU list, and the website's localized GBP prices differ materially from the US storefront.

verdictSummary: The core loop is small enough for a capable coding agent to produce a useful local version in one sitting. For PDF Expert, annotate, fill, merge, and lightly edit PDFs in a polished local desktop app. The hard boundary is native apple polish, sync, reliable rendering, and mobile continuity, plus document fidelity, identity, and compliance.
coreLoopDIY: Annotate, fill, merge, and lightly edit PDFs in a local desktop app, preserve originals, generate auditable outputs, and keep files in a user-owned store.
whatYouLose: native Apple polish, sync, reliable rendering, and mobile continuity
replacementScope: personal document tool or low-stakes signature flow
ongoingBurden: format edge cases, fonts, rendering, encryption, signatures, evidence, retention, storage, backups, and legal requirements
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for PDF Expert because the visible editor is reproducible, but reliable rendering and legally defensible signature workflows are not a casual side project. The recurring cost buys format edge cases, fonts, rendering, encryption, signatures, evidence, retention, storage, backups, and legal requirements, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Stirling PDF
priorArt.desc: Active open-source web application for a broad set of PDF operations.

alternatives.name: PDFgear
alternatives.desc: A polished free local editor for annotation, forms, signatures, merging, conversion, OCR, and light text edits; the most direct answer here.

alternatives.name: Preview
alternatives.desc: Already on every Mac and quietly excellent at viewing, annotating, filling, signing, rearranging, merging, and exporting PDFs; direct text editing is not the deal.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Premium plan and a personal document tool or low-stakes signature flow DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for PDF Expert in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, Python 3.12, FastAPI, pikepdf, LibreOffice headless, and PostgreSQL; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: annotate, fill, merge, and lightly edit PDFs in a local desktop app, preserve originals, generate auditable outputs, and keep files in a user-owned store.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Keep every original immutable and write each operation to a versioned output file.
Support merge, split, reorder, rotate, compress, watermark, redact, OCR, and Office-to-PDF conversion.
Render page previews and warn when fonts, forms, signatures, or encryption may be altered.
For signature mode, place fields, invite signers, record consent, and seal a final PDF hash.
Maintain an append-only event log with timestamps, document hashes, and delivery outcomes.
Add file expiry, download, deletion, backup, and a prominent low-stakes-use warning.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out qualified or regulated electronic signatures.
Deliberately leave out government identity verification.
Deliberately leave out full Acrobat-level editing and enterprise document governance.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
